Immediate Inferences, drawn

Executive brief · 25 October 2026 · Individuals/Nik Land/immediate-inferences-drawn.html

Bottom line

The new one-page application is built, and every one of its 101 passages has a figure beside it. It sits next to the old explorer, which I haven't changed: immediate-inferences.html and its data files are exactly as they were. The two pages link to each other and read the same examples and flag files.

The figures are checked, not just drawn. A small logic engine tests every judgement against the drawing its premise gives. It flagged exactly the two cases the earlier brief picked out by hand. One is Wiener's contraposition to a particular, where the figure shows more than the premise says. The other is Kant's rejected conversion in Refl. 3187, which picks out an empty region.

Nothing is committed. As the repository asks of local sessions, the new files are waiting for you in GitHub Desktop.

What it looks like

The figures, and why each looks as it does

Every kind of figure, and how many

FigureForPassages
SpheresConversion, contraposition, equipollence with an instance27
Square of oppositionContradictory, contrary, subcontrary, subalternation18
Spheres with a middle termThe three counter-examples3
Singular"diese Welt ist die beste", a point inside a sphere1
SchematicRules and definitions with no instance: the kind in general, in letters, dashed throughout52

On a phone (left) the figure moves under its passage and the panels stack. Each figure carries a text description for screen readers. Meaning is carried by line, label and pattern as well as colour, so it survives print and colour blindness.

How a figure is checked

Decisions, and why

DecisionWhy
A new file, beside the old explorerYou asked me not to delete the old one. The two pages share immediate-inference-examples.js, miscategorisations.js and diagram-flags.js, so a correction made once shows in both.
Figures inline, beside each passage, not in a pop-out panelThe earlier design repeats the geometry so figures can be compared. That only pays off if several are on screen at once. Here you can scroll the conversions and watch "Alle Menschen sind sterblich" turn round in Wiener, Busolt and the Reflexionen.
The navigation is Kant's map (Refl. 3170)It teaches the structure while it filters, and it is Kant's own sorting, not one I made up.
Attested and supplied kept apartThis is the repository's hard rule. Solid lines are the passage's, quoted exactly. Dashed lines are supplied: a premise not repeated, a converse left as "etc.", a contradictory not written out, the minor premise of a counter-example. Forms the passage doesn't name are in dashed boxes, and every concept name is marked as the annotator's.
Arrows on the square only for subalternationBetween opposites the square says what can be true together, not what follows. An arrow from I to O would claim an inference that no passage makes.
Reporting through a pre-filled GitHub issueThis is option A of the sync brief: no password in the page and no server. The issue carries the same kant-lab-flags-v1 data as the old explorer's, so the one workflow, once approved, can read both.
Pages worked out on load from the shared dataThe page reuses the old explorer's fix for the start-page bug in the transcript data. A re-run of the extractor therefore can't leave a stale AA page behind, and a quotation that stops matching is shown with a warning instead of vanishing.

How it was checked

Done

  • A syntax check of the page's script in JavaScriptCore.
  • Every figure drawn in headless Chrome: 101 of 101 rendered, none failed, all quotations found.
  • 21 scripted interaction tests: kind buttons, sources, search (umlauts ignored), hover-linking, the report dialog and its payload, links by hash, aria labels. All passed.
  • Screenshots at desktop and phone width, looked at and fixed. One real bug turned up: the stylesheet was overriding every label size in the figures.
  • The page's own citations checked against the data: Blomberg 24:275, Busolt 24:671, Wiener 24:938, Refl. 3170 and 3177.

Not done, or worth knowing

  • Not yet clicked through by a person in a normal browser. The checks above were scripted.
  • The 52 rule-only passages show the same schematic for their kind each time. That is deliberate, since every card gets a figure, but it is repetitive. It could fold away if you'd rather.
  • "Report a problem" opens the issue but can't write the flag files. That needs the sync brief's workflow in .github/, which the professor has to approve.
  • Concept names and subject–predicate readings come from the examples file, and they are the annotator's reading.
Decisions for you
  1. Keep both pages, or should this one take over from the old explorer's unfinished diagram panel?
  2. Commit the new page and the two briefs through GitHub Desktop?
  3. Ask the professor to approve the sync workflow, so reports land in the flag files by themselves?

New, uncommitted: immediate-inferences-drawn.html (about 1,660 lines, one file, no build step, opens by double-clicking), this brief, and request-failed-brief.html. Unchanged: immediate-inferences.html, immediate-inference-examples.js, miscategorisations.js, diagram-flags.js. The old explorer's earlier, uncommitted diagram-panel edits are still in your working tree as they were.
